correlation_memo: ONE FACTOR DOMINATES THE FUNNEL. Fourteen of twenty-nine names (CAPR, EYPT, MLYS, SRRK, DBVT, CELC, VRDN, AQST, WVE, AMLX, ZYME, VIR, OLMA, AVIR) are FDA/biotech and share a single resolution driver: agency decision risk multiplied by biotech beta, in a 2026 regime that has already produced pre-event briefing-package leaks (CAPR fell 64% on the document, two days before the advisory committee even met), favourable approvals the tape refused to pay for (CELC -17.6% ON approval; VRDN round-tripped its entire 12% pop inside a month), and cross-name pre-emption. Three of the six names I would seat sit inside this factor (ZYME, VIR, AVIR): seating all three is one bet with three tickets and should carry roughly ONE seat of aggregate weight, not three. The cluster label also hides a second-order contagion worth naming: EYPT and WVE were each killed not by their own regulator but by a COMPETITOR'S prior result in the same indication (Ocular Therapeutix's already-won wet-AMD pivotal; Beam's 11 Jan 2026 AATD pathway alignment). Within a single cluster, one rival's readout can delete two of your seats at once. BBIO, named in the cluster brief, has no live result file in this run and is not assessed. SECOND, SMALLER SHARED FACTOR: Chinese regulatory approval gates BOTH deal-completion names I would seat, DDL (SAMR anti-monopoly clearance of Meituan/Dingdong) and AAUC (Chinese outbound approval of Zijin/Allied Gold). Different agencies, different politics, but a common China-outbound-policy sensitivity: treat DDL plus AAUC as roughly 1.5 seats, not 2. PUREST STANDALONE ASYMMETRIES, in order. (1) DDL: the only downside in the funnel with a contractual component, a buyer-paid $0.35 per share break fee on top of about $2.03 per share of net cash against a $2.39 price, and a resolution driver shared with nothing else on the board except AAUC's China leg. (2) LBTYK: a Dutch cable spin under a sponsor with a completed template, EU-domiciled, orthogonal to oil, AI-capex, FDA and China alike, carrying the best raw ratio on the board at about 5.3 to 1, held back only by having no date. (3) AAUC: a signed all-cash gold deal whose only live risk is one named regulator, orthogonal to everything except gold, and gold is a falsification check in this stack rather than a scored input. (4) FIG: a contractual, dated share-supply event (7 Aug lock-up expiry) whose driver is pure mechanical float, though it is REFUTED on price. CAVEAT ON FIP: it looks idiosyncratic (FERC approval of a power-plant sale) but the buyer is MARA and the asset is datacenter-adjacent generation, so it carries real AI-capex beta and is NOT orthogonal to the factor resolving in the Jul 29-30 hyperscaler prints. Size it as a partial overlap, not a clean diversifier. The regime doc's rule #4 (enforce resolution-driver independence hard against BOTH oil/Hormuz and AI-capex) therefore binds on FIP specifically; none of the other seatable names touch either macro factor, which is the one genuinely favourable structural feature of this board.
memo:
THE HEADLINE, ANSWERED PLAINLY: ZERO names cleared the triple bar. Nine earned CRO verdict A (EYPT, FIP, MLYS, SRRK, ZYME, DDL, VIR, OLMA, AVIR). Two earned CRO conviction 5 (ZYME, VIR). NONE earned a Director score of 80 or above. The top of the board is ZYME at 78, then VIR at 74. The 407-name drought the priced-quality funnels have never broken is intact after twenty-nine event-driven names, and the reason this run produces is a structural finding rather than a failure of nerve.

WHY NOTHING REACHED 80. The 80-plus band needs three things at once: an imminent hard date, a large live-to-target spread, and a defined floor. Across this funnel those three are ANTI-CORRELATED, and the anti-correlation is the market working rather than the analysts failing. Every name with a huge spread has a soft floor or a soft date: VIR +116% on a quarter-wide window and a burn-adjusted cash mark, FIP +113% on a levered stub with no backstop at all, LBTYK +88% with no date whatsoever, AVIR +87% with a floor the skeptic cut by 13% on omitted current liabilities. Every name with a hard date and a real-ish floor has almost no spread: ZYME +26%, GDOT +8.1%, UNF +6.9%, AXTA +3.5% and actually NEGATIVE on corrected inputs. The single name with a part-contractual floor, DDL, has the softest regulator clock on the board. Where the market gives you a date it takes the spread; where it gives you a spread it takes the floor. That is this run's most portable conclusion, and it is a lane-level statement, not a name-level one.

SECOND FINDING, AND IT IS AN INTAKE DEFECT WORTH FIXING BEFORE THE NEXT RUN. The skeptic layer struck down or materially cut the recorded downside_floor in at least fourteen of twenty-nine names, and in four cases the floor had ALREADY BROKEN on the tape: CAPR ($7.00 breached to $6.995 on the briefing package, before the advisory committee met), FIG ($17.50 breached at $16.60 in June), PRX.AS (37.365 breached, 36.17 low), FUN ($16.50 breached at $12.51). MP's $35 and $32, KDP's $28.50, GDOT's $11.00, LZM's $2.60, AMLX's $3.00, OLMA's $4.25 and AVIR's $2.00 were all shown to be chart levels, moving averages, forward cash forecasts or wrong-share-count arithmetic wearing a floor-shaped field. This is systematic, not unlucky: the funnel records modelled marks in a field whose name promises a contract. Until the field distinguishes CONTRACTUAL (break fee, cash tender, appraisal right, net cash after ALL liabilities) from MODELLED, no name in this lane can honestly clear the hard-floor leg of the 90-100 band, and the 80-plus band will keep failing on the same leg regardless of how good the events get.

THIRD FINDING: THE FIRED NAMES ARE THE LANE'S REAL LESSON. Four catalysts resolved FAVOURABLY inside the window and the tape paid for none of them. CELC got a full approval three days early and fell 17.6% the next session. VRDN got approval four days early with a broader label than expected, no advisory committee and no CRL, and round-tripped the whole 12% pop inside a month. PRX.AS completed a regulator-forced divestment at successive premiums and the re-rating accrued to the target's shareholders, leaving about EUR 0.09 per share settling in H2-2027. THRM's antitrust clearance landed four months before the review date and was never an arb to begin with, because Gentherm is the acquirer and issuer in a Reverse Morris Trust and no counterparty ever contracted to pay a THRM holder anything. That is 0-for-4 on 'the event went our way.' It corroborates the Catalyst-Watch v4 read that the hard-binary lane is thinnest of the six for a third consecutive run, and it argues the sleeve's edge, if it has one, lives in the mechanical forced-seller and spin archetypes the regime doc ranks #1, not in the FDA archetype that supplied fourteen of these twenty-nine candidates.

WHAT I WOULD SEAT: six names. ZYME (78), VIR (74), FIP (68), DDL (67), AVIR (66), AAUC (64). All sit in the solid-to-high-conviction bands, none is table-pounding, and per the correlation memo the three biotechs among them should be sized as roughly one seat and DDL plus AAUC as roughly 1.5. ZYME is the closest thing to a genuine aggressive entry the funnel produced: a 28-day statutory PDUFA on a label expansion of an already-approved, partner-marketed drug whose Phase 3 met both primary endpoints across 914 patients and was published in the NEJM, releasing a fixed, unpledged $250m contractual milestone on approval, with the skeptic returning an explicit no-kill after attacking all four vectors. It is held at 78 by two honest facts rather than by timidity: +26% is not a large spread for a binary that can also go to $18, and the floor's cash plank rests on a Theravance close that may land after the event. VIR is the best pure asymmetry with a real cash backstop (62% of the price is net cash) but its window is a quarter rather than a day, and the skeptic struck the timeline-upgrade argument that was doing the incremental work in the bull case.

REGIME OVERLAY ON THE SEATING. The v4 read has the oil/Hormuz tripwire BREACHED with VIX 18.5 and HY 271bp conspicuously not confirming, so gap risk is underpriced and these names should be sized for overnight-gap regimes rather than grind regimes, which matters because five of the six seatable names can move 40% or more on a single headline. The Jul 28-30 cluster (FOMC, then MSFT/META and AAPL/AMZN capex verdicts) argues for letting anything resolving inside it land before adding: that spares ZYME (25 Aug), VIR (Q4), DDL (undated) and AAUC (post-extension), but argues for staging FIP around its 5 Aug print and the FERC order rather than taking a full seat now, and for staging AVIR, whose guided window has just lapsed and could print straight into the cluster. The DISCIPLINE debt-cycle phase is ADVISORY here under EQUAL_WEIGHT_BOOKS and moves no published weight; its only live effect is the 18-month horizon stretch, which is the right horizon for LBTYK's mid-2027 spin and DDL's Feb-2027 longstop and is binding on nothing else on this board. Note for the ledger: the duration_bucket for this whole sleeve is story or unknown almost throughout, since event-driven names carry no p_fcf, so the cycle caps would bind hard here if EQUAL_WEIGHT_BOOKS were ever flipped off.

ONE OVERTURN WORTH RECORDING. The FIG skeptic explicitly reversed a prior shard that had killed the name on a false fact, namely that the Extended Lock-Up Agreement 'does not exist,' reasoned from the absence of an 8-K on a Saturday. The catalyst is real, contractual and dated to 7 August. FIG still scores 46 because it is REFUTED on the floor and on price, not on existence, but that 7 Aug supply event is the single cleanest mechanical forced-seller date on this board and belongs on the watch list for an entry below the June low, which is precisely the archetype the regime doc ranks fattest and precisely the archetype this funnel is under-sourcing.
